text.title: Node.js Service Layer Architecture Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a second transport will ever run the logic, then on where the database access lives today and which concern is leaking across a boundary, to the rule that fixes the next move.

decision-tree.root-question: Will any transport other than HTTP — queue worker, cron job, CLI, webhook consumer — ever execute this logic, and does the code own business rules of its own rather than forwarding to another API?

branch.when: pass-through BFF with no rules of its own, or HTTP is the only consumer that will ever exist

conclusion.verdict: skip; the layering buys reachability from a second transport and database-free tests, and neither is on offer — emit a structured skip naming which condition held

branch.when: a second consumer exists or is planned, or the code owns real domain rules
branch.question: Where does database access live in the code today?

branch.when: route handlers query the ORM directly; there is no service layer
branch.question: Does any single request write to two or more tables or aggregates, or call an external service alongside its writes?

branch.when: yes; a unit of work spans several writes, sometimes with an HTTP or LLM call between them

conclusion.verdict: open the transaction in the service and thread the tx client through every repository call; move external calls outside the callback before extracting anything else

branch.when: no; single-write handlers, but the same ORM calls are already copy-pasted into a worker or cron

conclusion.verdict: extract to a service so one rule serves both transports, and pin it with an ESLint no-restricted-imports ban on ORM identifiers under controllers

branch.when: a service layer exists but concerns leak across its boundaries
branch.question: What crosses a boundary that should not?

branch.when: repository or service signatures return ORM-generated types (Prisma.UserGetPayload, User from @prisma/client)

conclusion.verdict: declare domain types in the module and stop ORM imports at the repository, so a service test can construct input without the schema

branch.when: services import shared singletons at module level (prisma, stripe) instead of receiving them

conclusion.verdict: pass repositories and clients as constructor or factory arguments; a module-registry substitution is process-wide and makes parallel test files share a double

branch.when: services reference res or throw numeric HTTP statuses

conclusion.verdict: throw typed domain errors with a stable code and map code to status in exactly one error middleware, so the queue consumer can share the service

branch.when: the layers look right but nothing mechanically stops a repository importing a service

conclusion.verdict: wire dependency-cruiser or no-restricted-paths into CI and name the config file in the artefact; CommonJS require cycles fail by entry point, not by test

branch.when: greenfield; no layering exists yet and the boundaries are still open

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; emit the layer map, transaction ownership and error taxonomy as an artefact with status=ready_for_review
